definition_en: the vast body of salt water that surrounds the continents and covers most of the earth

scene: 地理课上，老师转动地球仪，指着连成一片的蓝色说，A single ocean can hold more water than all the land it surrounds.
sceneCN: 这里 ocean 指「地球上环绕陆地的巨大咸水体」（第 1 个义项：连成整体、覆盖大部分地表的咸水）；句意为：一个海洋能容纳的水量超过它周围全部陆地。

senses.title: The world-encircling body of salt water
senses.titleCN: 覆盖地球大部分表面的连片咸水
senses.definition: the great body of salt water that surrounds the continents and covers most of the planet
senses.definitionCN: 环绕各大陆、覆盖地球大部分表面的巨大咸水体
senses.example: A single ocean can hold more water than all the land it surrounds.
senses.exampleCN: 一个海洋能容纳的水量超过它周围全部陆地。
senses.why: Greek Okeanos named the stream believed to run all the way around the world, so the word began as one continuous encircling water, not as a list of separate seas.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 Okeanos 原本指绕世界一周的大河，所以这个词从诞生起就是「一圈连着的咸水」，而非若干彼此分开的海。

senses.title: One of the named divisions
senses.titleCN: 五大洋中一个有名字的洋
senses.definition: one of the five large divisions of this water, such as the Pacific, Atlantic or Indian ocean
senses.definitionCN: 这片水域被划分出的五大洋之一，如太平洋、大西洋或印度洋
senses.example: The Atlantic ocean narrows toward its northern end.
senses.exampleCN: 大西洋在它的北端变窄。
senses.why: once geographers divided the single world water into named basins, the same word served both the whole and each part, and context decides which is meant.
senses.whyCN: 地理学家把这一整片世界水域划分成有名字的海盆之后，同一个词既指整体也指其中一部分，靠上下文决定所指。

senses.title: The water as opposed to the land
senses.definition: the open salt water thought of as a place distinct from land, especially in travel and trade
senses.definitionCN: 与陆地相对的开阔咸水，尤用于航行与贸易语境
senses.example: They spent three weeks on the ocean before sighting land.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海上待了三个星期才看见陆地。
senses.why: a voyage needs two settings, land and water; the word supplies the second one, so 'on the ocean' simply means out on the salt water.
senses.whyCN: 一次远航需要两个场景：陆地与水面；这个词提供后者，因此「在海洋上」就是身处开阔咸水之中。

senses.title: A very large amount
senses.definition: an immense quantity of something, especially something abstract such as words or work
senses.definitionCN: 某事物数量极大，尤指话语、工作等抽象事物
senses.example: An ocean of paperwork awaited the new clerk.
senses.exampleCN: 海量的文书工作等着这位新职员。
senses.why: the figurative step is simple: the largest thing most speakers know becomes the measure of anything too big to count, so an ocean of forms is just too many forms.
senses.whyCN: 比喻的跳跃很简单：把说话人知道的最大之物拿来度量多到数不清的东西，因此「一整个海洋的表格」就是表格多到数不清。

senses.title: A boundless expanse
senses.definition: a vast unbroken stretch of something that seems to have no edge, such as sand or grass
senses.definitionCN: 沙、草等铺展到看不见边界的广阔一片
senses.example: An ocean of sand stretched from the road to the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 一片沙海从路边一直铺到地平线。
senses.why: the eye reads any surface without a visible edge the way it reads water, so desert and prairie borrow the word for the same feeling of no boundary.
senses.whyCN: 人眼看到没有可见边界的表面时，读法与看水面一样，因此沙漠与草原借这个词表达同样的「无边」之感。

senses.title: A depth of feeling
senses.definition: an overwhelming quantity of a feeling that seems to swallow a person up
senses.definitionCN: 铺天盖地、仿佛把人吞没的情感
senses.example: She sank into an ocean of grief after the funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 葬礼之后，她沉入一片悲痛的汪洋。
senses.why: deep water is the standing image for what cannot be crossed or controlled, so grief and doubt are described as oceans, with the person inside them rather than beside them.
senses.whyCN: 深水一直是无从跨越、无法掌控的意象，因此悲伤与疑虑被说成海洋，而人是在其中，不在其旁。

senses.title: The ocean as a climate system
senses.definition: the salt water regarded as a system that stores heat, moves currents and regulates the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 把咸水视为储存热量、驱动洋流并调节大气的一个系统
senses.example: The ocean absorbs much of the heat trapped by greenhouse gases.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋吸收了温室气体截留的大部分热量。
senses.why: twentieth-century earth science turned the place into a mechanism: the same water that sails are built for is now studied as a store and pump of heat.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪的地球科学把这个地点变成了机制：原本造船航行的同一片水，如今被当作热量的储库与泵来研究。

senses.title: The high seas in law
senses.definition: open water beyond any state's coastal jurisdiction, belonging to no single country
senses.definitionCN: 超出任何国家沿海管辖范围、不属任何一国所有的开阔水域
senses.example: Beyond the twelve-mile limit lies the open ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 越过十二海里界限，就是开阔的公海。
senses.why: maritime law needed a term for water that no flag claims; the everyday word for the great water took that legal slot without changing shape.
senses.whyCN: 海商法需要一个词指没有任何国旗主张的水域，于是日常指大水的词原样填进了这个法律位置。

senses.title: Ocean as a shipping modifier
senses.definition: used before another noun to mean carried by, used on, or belonging to the open sea
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示由远洋承运、用于远洋或属于远洋的
senses.example: Ocean freight moves most goods between continents.
senses.exampleCN: 远洋货运承担了洲际间的大部分货物。
senses.why: when a noun is placed before another noun it stops naming a place and starts naming a route or a class, which is how ocean becomes the label on a shipping container.
senses.whyCN: 名词放到另一个名词前时，它不再指地点，而开始指一条路线或一个类别，海洋就是这样变成了集装箱上的运输标签。

intro.en: Ocean reaches English through Latin and Old French from Greek Okeanos, the name of the stream that was thought to run around the whole inhabited world. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ocean 经拉丁语与古法语进入英语，源头是希腊语 Okeanos——古人想象中环绕整个已知世界的大河之名。年代均为约数。

items.en: Okeanos in Homer is the river that encircles the disc of the world and is never crossed; it is a proper name first, a common noun for the outer water later.
items.cn: 荷马笔下的 Okeanos 是环绕世界圆盘、无人能越的大河；它先是专名，后来才成为指外围水域的普通名词。

items.en: Later Greek writers, above all Herodotus, used okeanos for the open water outside the Mediterranean, and the word began to mean the sea itself rather than a river.
items.cn: 后来的希腊作者，尤其是希罗多德，用 okeanos 指地中海之外的开阔水域，这个词开始表示海本身而非一条河。

items.en: Latin took Oceanus as both a name and a common noun for the great sea; the adjective oceanicus 'of the ocean' follows the same stem.
items.cn: 拉丁语把 Oceanus 同时用作专名与指大海洋的普通名词；形容词 oceanicus「海洋的」沿用同一词干。

items.en: Old French occean passed the word to Middle English around the fourteenth century, where it first named the outer sea and only later any large body of salt water.
items.cn: 古法语 occean 在 14 世纪前后把这个词传给中古英语，最初指外围的大海，后来才泛指任何巨大咸水体。

items.en: From the age of exploration the single world water was mapped as named oceans, and the older 'stream around the world' image survives only in poetry and etymology.
items.cn: 从大航海时代起，这一整片世界水域被绘制成有名字的几个大洋，古老「绕世大河」的意象只留在诗歌与词源说明里。

items.en: Source uncertain (root origin, not first date): the deeper origin of Greek Okeanos is disputed, with some scholars treating it as a pre-Greek loan; any reconstructed Indo-European form for it is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指词根来源，不是首见年代）：希腊语 Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，有学者视之为前希腊语借词；为它构拟的任何印欧语形式都只是假说，不是已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like ocean or are built on the same stem; group two holds words for water that differ in size or register.
note.cn: 第一组是与 ocean 形近或同出同一词干的词；第二组是都指水域、但规模或语体不同的词。

entries.definition: the collective name for the Pacific islands and Australia; it adds -ia to the Oceanus stem, so it names a region, not a body of water.
entries.definitionCN: 太平洋岛屿与澳大利亚的合称；在 Oceanus 词干上加 -ia，指一个区域，而不是一片水域。

entries.definition: ocean plus -ic: relating to the ocean, or simply very large and open, as in oceanic distances.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -ic：与海洋有关的，或形容极其辽阔开阔的，如「远洋般的距离」。

entries.definition: ocean plus -graphy 'writing, describing': the scientific study of the sea, not the sea itself.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 -graphy「书写、描述」：对海洋的科学研究，而不是海洋本身。

entries.definition: ocean plus front: land that faces the sea, so the compound names property rather than water.
entries.definitionCN: ocean 加 front：面朝大海的陆地，因此这个复合词指地产，而非水域。

entries.definition: a body of salt water smaller than an ocean and often partly enclosed by land; the everyday word for the water you can see from a shore.
entries.definitionCN: 比大洋小、常被陆地部分围住的咸水体；指岸边看得见的那片水的日常用词。

entries.definition: a plural used for a particular stretch of water, as in territorial waters; it is neutral in size and common in law and news.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式，指某一片特定水域，如领海；不限定规模，常见于法律与新闻。

entries.definition: an old poetic word for the open sea, as in the Spanish Main; it survives mostly in verse and historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 指开阔大海的古雅诗歌用词，如「西班牙海」；如今多存于诗歌与历史写作。

entries.definition: the deep is a literary name for the sea that stresses its depth rather than its width; it fits images of sinking and hiding.
entries.definitionCN: the deep 是海洋的文学称呼，强调深度而非广度；适合「沉没、隐藏」一类意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek Okeanos was the river around the world, so the word began as one continuous ring of water.
normal.cn: 希腊语 Okeanos 是绕世界的大河，因此这个词最初就是一圈连着的水。

normal.en: The family runs ocean, oceanic, oceanography, oceanographer, oceanarium, oceanfront.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ocean、oceanic、oceanography、oceanographer、oceanarium、oceanfront。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical sense: ocean floor, ocean basin, deep ocean, open ocean.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：海底、海盆、深海、开阔洋面。

normal.en: Geography names five: the Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern and Arctic oceans.
normal.cn: 地理学列出五个：太平洋、大西洋、印度洋、南大洋与北冰洋。

normal.en: The idiom an ocean of means a huge amount, as in an ocean of paperwork.
normal.cn: 短语 an ocean of 表示极多，如海量文书。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of water that cannot find a shore to belong to.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴水找不到可以归属的岸。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the blue is not a colour but a distance you cannot cross.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，上面的蓝色不是颜色，而是一段跨不过去的距离。

abstract.en: Picture a voice heard across water, arriving in layers like waves.
abstract.cn: 想象隔着水传来的人声，一层一层像浪一样抵达。

examples.en: The ocean covers about seventy percent of the earth's surface.
examples.cn: 海洋覆盖了地球表面约七成。

examples.en: Scientists track how the ocean moves heat from the tropics poleward.
examples.cn: 科学家追踪海洋如何把热量从热带向极地输送。

examples.en: From the cliff we watched an ocean of cloud roll inland.
examples.cn: 从崖上望去，我们看着一片云海向内陆翻滚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，深海」——看到望不到边的水，先「哦」一声，再想到深海大洋 → 海洋、大量

root: 希腊 Okeanos「环绕世界的大河」（专名转普通名词）→ 拉丁 Oceanus → 古法语 occean → 英语 ocean；Okeanos 的更早来源有争议，或为前希腊语借词，构拟的印欧形式均属假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses radiate from one picture: a ring of salt water around the land, then the named parts, the water seen from a ship, the same boundlessness borrowed for quantity and feeling, and finally the water studied as a machine and claimed in law.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从同一个画面辐射出去：环绕陆地的咸水圈，然后是其中命名分区、船上所见的水面，同一份「无边」被借去指数量与情感，最后是当作机器研究的海洋与法律主张的海域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous ring of salt water holding the land inside it, too wide to see across.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整圈连着的咸水把陆地围在里面，宽到看不见对岸。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BODY: the same water is first a place on the map and later a heat store studied by climate science.
branches.cn: 物理水体：同一片水先是地图上的一个地点，后来成为气候科学研究的储热系统。

branches.en: DIVIDED AND CLAIMED: geography cuts the whole into named oceans, and law marks where national claims stop.
branches.cn: 被划分与被主张：地理学把整体切成有名字的洋，法律标出国家主张止于何处。

branches.en: SEEN FROM A SHIP: from deck the water is a setting for travel, and as a modifier it labels the freight that crosses it.
branches.cn: 从船上看见：在甲板上水是旅行的场景，作定语时则标注穿越它的货运。

branches.en: BORROWED SCALE: the widest thing a speaker knows measures paperwork, sand and grass.
branches.cn: 借来的尺度：说话人知道的最宽之物，被用来度量文书、沙与草。

branches.en: INWARD WATER: grief and doubt become oceans because the person is inside them, not beside them.
branches.cn: 向内的水：悲伤与疑虑变成海洋，因为人是在其中，而不是在其旁。

intro.en: Ocean is a borrowed proper name that became a common noun; its family is built with Greek and Latin suffixes added to the same stem.
intro.cn: ocean 是一个转为普通名词的外来专名；它的词族都是在同一词干上加希腊语与拉丁语后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Latin Oceanus keeps both the name and the common noun, and oceanicus supplies the adjective pattern behind oceanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 Oceanus 同时保留专名与普通名词用法，oceanicus 则提供了 oceanic 背后的形容词构词模式。

items.meaning: the stream believed to encircle the world
items.meaningCN: 古人想象中环绕世界的大河
items.example: Homer places Okeanos at the rim of the known world.
items.exampleCN: 荷马把 Okeanos 放在已知世界的边缘。

items.example: The ocean covers most of the planet.
items.exampleCN: 海洋覆盖了地球的大部分。

items.example: Oceanic currents redistribute heat.
items.exampleCN: 洋流重新分配热量。

items.meaning: the scientific description of the sea
items.meaningCN: 对海洋的科学描述与研究
items.example: Oceanography combines chemistry, physics and biology.
items.exampleCN: 海洋学结合了化学、物理学与生物学。

items.meaning: a person who studies the sea
items.example: The oceanographer lowered a probe to the trench floor.
items.exampleCN: 海洋学家把探测器下放到海沟底部。

items.meaning: a large enclosure for living sea animals
items.meaningCN: 饲养活体海洋动物的大型场馆
items.example: The oceanarium rebuilt its reef tank.
items.exampleCN: 这座海洋馆重建了珊瑚礁展缸。

items.example: Oceanfront lots sold out within a week.
items.exampleCN: 临海地块一周内售罄。

items.meaning: built for crossing the open sea
items.example: The yard launched an ocean-going tug.
items.exampleCN: 船厂下水了一艘远洋拖船。

items.meaning: the island region of the Pacific
items.example: Oceania includes thousands of islands.
items.exampleCN: 大洋洲包含成千上万座岛屿。

latinEntries.meaning: the great outer sea; also its divine name
latinEntries.meaningCN: 外围的大海；亦为海神之名

latinEntries.structure: oceanicus, oceanica, oceanicum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 海的；海运的；沿海的；海事的
definition_en: relating to the sea, to shipping, or to activities that take place on or near the sea
core_image: 一艘船从岸边驶向远海，船与岸之间连着航线、规则和一条看不见的边界
scene: 在港口值班室里，管理员翻开厚厚一叠卷宗说，Every maritime dispute in this port is recorded here.
sceneCN: 这里 maritime 指「与海运、海事有关的」（第 3 个义项：海事法律的）；句意为：这个港口的每一起海事纠纷都记录在这里。

forms.label: 比较级（罕用，关系形容词通常不比较）

senses.title: Belonging to the sea in general
senses.definition: connected with the sea as a physical place, including its plants, animals and weather
senses.definitionCN: 与作为物理场所的海洋有关，包括其中的动植物与天气
senses.example: The museum collects maritime fossils from shallow sea beds.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆收集来自浅海床的海洋化石。
senses.why: Latin maritimus means 'of the sea', built on mare 'sea', so the adjective begins as a plain label for anything the sea supplies.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 maritimus 意为「海的」，由 mare「海」构成，因此这个形容词一开始就是给海洋所提供的一切贴的标签。

senses.title: Connected with shipping
senses.definition: connected with ships, ports and the business of carrying goods by water
senses.definitionCN: 与船舶、港口以及水上货运业务有关
senses.example: Maritime trade made the city rich long before the railway arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 早在铁路出现之前，海上贸易就让这座城市富了起来。
senses.why: once goods moved mainly by water, everything the sea carried became maritime, so the word shifted from the water itself to the industry built on it.
senses.whyCN: 货物曾主要走水路，凡由海承运之事都归入 maritime，这个词于是从水域本身转向建立在水域上的产业。

senses.title: Belonging to maritime law
senses.definition: connected with the law and courts that deal with ships, crews, cargo and accidents at sea
senses.definitionCN: 与处理船舶、船员、货物及海上事故的法律和法庭有关
senses.example: Every maritime dispute in this port is recorded here.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口的每一起海事纠纷都记录在这里。
senses.why: ships cross borders and carry other people's goods, so a body of rules had to follow them onto the water; the adjective marks that separate legal world.
senses.whyCN: 船舶跨越国界、载着别人的货物，因此必须有一套规则跟着它们上船；这个形容词标记的就是那个独立的法律世界。

senses.title: Situated on the coast
senses.definition: located on or close to the coast, especially a province, city or region
senses.definitionCN: 位于海岸之上或附近，尤指省份、城市或地区
senses.example: Maritime provinces depend on fishing and tourism.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海省份依靠渔业与旅游业。
senses.why: a place that faces the sea shares its weather, its work and its history, so the adjective moves from the water to the land that looks at it.
senses.whyCN: 面朝大海的地方共享海的气候、生计与历史，因此这个形容词从水域移到了望着水域的陆地。

senses.title: Maritime climate
senses.titleCN: 受海洋调节的海洋性气候
senses.definition: describing a climate with mild winters, cool summers and steady moisture because the sea moderates it
senses.definitionCN: 形容冬季温和、夏季凉爽、湿度稳定，因海洋起到调节作用的气候
senses.example: The island's maritime climate keeps frost away almost every year.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛的海洋性气候几乎年年都不结霜。
senses.why: water warms and cools more slowly than rock, so a coast is never as extreme as an inland plain; the adjective names that moderating effect.
senses.whyCN: 水比岩石升温降温都慢，因此沿海从不像内陆平原那样极端；这个形容词命名的正是这种调节作用。

senses.title: A named coastal region
senses.definition: used as part of a proper name for a coastal area, as in the Maritime Provinces of Canada
senses.definitionCN: 用作沿海地区专名的一部分，如加拿大的沿海诸省
senses.example: She grew up in a small town in the Maritimes.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一个沿海小城长大。
senses.why: the plural noun maritimes turns the adjective into a place name, a habit English has with several coastal regions.
senses.whyCN: 复数名词 maritimes 把这个形容词变成地名，英语对若干沿海地区都有这种用法。

senses.title: Sea power of a state
senses.definition: describing the naval and commercial strength of a country that depends on the sea
senses.definitionCN: 形容依赖海洋的国家的海军与商业实力
senses.example: The report compares maritime powers across the Indian Ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 该报告比较印度洋沿岸各海上强国的实力。
senses.why: a nation that lives by trade and navies is strong precisely where the sea is, so maritime becomes a shorthand for that kind of power.
senses.whyCN: 靠贸易与海军立国的国家，其力量恰在海上，因此 maritime 成了这类实力的简称。

senses.title: A sea boundary between states
senses.definition: connected with the line at sea that separates the waters claimed by two states
senses.definitionCN: 与两国所主张水域之间的海上分界线有关
senses.example: The two neighbours finally signed a maritime boundary agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个邻国终于签署了海上边界协定。
senses.why: land borders are drawn on maps, but sea borders must be negotiated over water, so the adjective marks this special kind of line.
senses.whyCN: 陆地边界画在地图上，海上边界却要在水面上谈判，因此这个形容词标记这种特殊的界线。

senses.title: Sea heritage and tradition
senses.definition: connected with the history, crafts and customs of people who have lived by the sea
senses.definitionCN: 与靠海生活的人的历史、手艺与习俗有关
senses.example: The festival keeps maritime songs and boat-building skills alive.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节庆让海上歌谣与造船技艺得以延续。
senses.why: when the industry fades, what remains is memory, and the same adjective now protects the songs and skills rather than the trade.
senses.whyCN: 产业衰退之后留下的是记忆，同一个形容词如今保护的是歌谣与技艺，而不是贸易。

intro.en: Maritime comes from Latin maritimus 'of the sea', a derivative of mare 'sea', and entered English through French in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: maritime 来自拉丁 maritimus「海的」，由 mare「海」派生，16 世纪经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Mare is the ordinary Latin word for the sea, neuter of the third declension; it also appears in names such as Mare Nostrum, 'our sea', for the Mediterranean.
items.cn: mare 是拉丁语中指海的常用词，属第三变格中性名词；也出现在 Mare Nostrum「我们的海」这类指地中海的名称中。

items.en: Maritimus 'of the sea, coastal' is built on mare with the adjective suffix -timus, the same ending seen in finitimus 'neighbouring'.
items.cn: maritimus「海的、沿海的」由 mare 加形容词后缀 -timus 构成，finitimus「毗邻的」也带同一词尾。

items.en: A second adjective, marinus, was formed with -inus instead; it produced English marine and mariner, which is why the two families look alike but follow different suffixes.
items.cn: 另一个形容词 marinus 用的是 -inus 后缀；它产生了英语 marine 与 mariner，这也解释了为何两族词形相近却走了不同后缀。

items.en: French maritime carried the Latin adjective into English in the sixteenth century, first in legal and geographical writing about sea boundaries and coastal provinces.
items.cn: 法语 maritime 在 16 世纪把这个拉丁形容词带入英语，最初见于关于海上边界与沿海省份的法律、地理写作。

items.en: Modern English extended the word from coast and law to shipping, climate and heritage, while the plural Maritimes became a proper name for Canada's Atlantic provinces.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词从海岸与法律扩展到航运、气候与文化遗产，复数 the Maritimes 则成为加拿大沿大西洋诸省的专名。

items.en: Partly uncertain: the deeper origin of mare is reconstructed as Indo-European *mori- 'sea', a form found only by comparison and not attested; the exact earlier function of the suffix -timus is also debated, so the analysis is generally accepted rather than proved.
items.cn: 部分存疑：mare 的更早来源被重构为印欧语 *mori-「海」，这一形式仅靠比较得出，并无文献佐证；后缀 -timus 更早的确切功能也有争议，因此上述分析属于「一般认为是」，并非已证实。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like maritime but do not all share its root; group two holds adjectives that also describe the sea from different angles.
note.cn: 第一组是与 maritime 形近、但并非都同源的词；第二组是从不同角度描写海洋的形容词。

entries.definition: from Latin marinus, the -inus adjective of mare: it describes what lives in or belongs to the sea, as in marine biology.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 marinus，即 mare 的 -inus 形容词：描写生活在海中或属于海洋的事物，如海洋生物学。

entries.definition: a sailor, literally 'one of the sea', built on marinus plus -er; it names a person, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 水手，字面是「属于海的人」，由 marinus 加 -er 构成；它指人，不指性质。

entries.definition: from Latin maritus 'husband', not mare: it means relating to marriage, so it is a look-alike only and has no connection with the sea.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」，而非 mare：意为与婚姻有关的，因此只是形近，与海洋毫无词源关系。

entries.definition: the adjective turned into a plural place name for coastal provinces, chiefly Canada's Atlantic provinces.
entries.definitionCN: 把这个形容词变成复数地名，指沿海诸省，主要指加拿大沿大西洋的省份。

entries.definition: from Greek nautes 'sailor': it describes navigation, measurements and skills of sailing rather than the sea as a place.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 nautes「水手」：描写航行、测量与航海技能，而非作为场所的海洋。

entries.definition: from Latin navis 'ship': it belongs to a country's warships and navy, a narrower military slice of maritime.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 navis「船」：属于一个国家的军舰与海军，是 maritime 中较窄的军事部分。

entries.definition: a native English compound meaning travelling or working by sea; it sounds older and more human than the Latin adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 英语本族复合词，意为以海为生、在海上航行工作；比这个拉丁形容词更古老、更有人情味。

entries.definition: of the open ocean rather than the coast or the shipping business; it stresses vast water and its life, not ports and law.
entries.definitionCN: 指开阔大洋而非海岸或航运业；强调辽阔水域及其生命，而非港口与法律。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin mare 'sea' gives maritimus, marinus and the English family marine, mariner, maritime.
normal.cn: 拉丁 mare「海」衍生出 maritimus、marinus，以及英语的 marine、mariner、maritime。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: maritime law, maritime trade, maritime climate, maritime boundary.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把义项分开：海事法、海上贸易、海洋性气候、海上边界。

normal.en: The -timus suffix also appears in finitimus 'neighbouring', which marks a boundary.
normal.cn: 后缀 -timus 也出现在 finitimus「毗邻的」中，同样带有边界意味。

normal.en: Maritime law is the branch that follows a ship across borders.
normal.cn: 海事法是跟着船舶跨越国界的那一支法律。

normal.en: The Maritimes is a proper name, so the plural noun is capitalised.
normal.cn: the Maritimes 是专名，因此复数名词要大写。

abstract.en: Picture a rope thrown from shore to ship, taut with rules as much as with fibre.
abstract.cn: 想象一根从岸上抛向船的缆绳，绷紧的不只是纤维，还有规则。

abstract.en: Picture a map where the border runs across open water with no fence to mark it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图，边界横穿开阔水面，没有任何栅栏来标记。

abstract.en: Picture an old song carried further than the boat that first sang it.
abstract.cn: 想象一首老歌比最先唱它的船走得更远。

examples.en: Maritime trade linked the port to markets across three continents.
examples.cn: 海上贸易把这个港口与三大洲的市场连在一起。

examples.en: The court applied maritime law to the collision in fog.
examples.cn: 法院对这起雾中碰撞适用了海事法。

examples.en: A maritime climate keeps the valley green into late autumn.
examples.cn: 海洋性气候让这条谷地一直到深秋都保持青绿。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马里太木」——马里港口的木头船靠海运出海 → 海运的、海事的、沿海的

root: 拉丁 mare「海」+ 形容词后缀 -timus → maritimus「海的、沿海的」→ 法语 maritime → 英语 maritime；同根另有 marinus（→ marine、mariner），两者后缀不同。mare 的印欧来源 *mori- 为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses spread outward from one shore: the sea itself, the shipping built on it, the law that follows ships, the coast that faces it, the climate it moderates, the region named after it, the power it gives, the border drawn across it, and the memory left behind.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一道海岸向外铺开：海本身、建立在海上的航运、跟着船走的法律、面朝海的陆地、由海调节的气候、以海命名的地区、海赋予的实力、横穿海面的边界，以及最后留下的记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ship leaving a shore, with routes, rules and an invisible border stretched between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一艘船离岸驶向远海，船与岸之间张着航线、规则与一条看不见的边界。

branches.en: WATER AND WORK: the adjective first labels the sea's own life, then the industry that carries goods across it.
branches.cn: 水与生计：这个形容词先标注海中生命，再标注跨海运货的产业。

branches.en: RULES OVER WATER: courts follow ships across borders, and states must negotiate a line no fence can mark.
branches.cn: 水面上的规则：法庭跟着船跨越国界，国家则要谈判一条没有栅栏可标记的线。

branches.en: THE LAND THAT FACES IT: coast and province borrow the adjective, and the plural turns it into a place name.
branches.cn: 望着海的陆地：海岸与省份借用这个形容词，复数形式则把它变成地名。

branches.en: WHAT THE SEA LEAVES: it moderates the air above the coast and later survives as songs and skills.
branches.cn: 海留下什么：它调节海岸上方的空气，后来又以歌谣与技艺留存。

branches.en: POWER: a state that lives by trade and navies concentrates its strength exactly where the sea is.
branches.cn: 实力：靠贸易与海军立国的国家，把力量恰好集中在海上。

intro.en: Maritime is a Latin adjective, not a native compound: its pieces are the noun mare, the suffix -timus, and a French carrier that brought it into English.
intro.cn: maritime 是拉丁形容词，不是英语本族复合词：它的构件是名词 mare、后缀 -timus，以及把它带进英语的法语中介。

latinIntro.en: Latin mare yields maritimus and marinus; the first gives maritime, the second gives marine, mariner and submarine.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mare 衍生 maritimus 与 marinus；前者给出 maritime，后者给出 marine、mariner 与 submarine。

items.example: Mare Nostrum was the Roman name for the Mediterranean.
items.exampleCN: Mare Nostrum 是罗马人对地中海的称呼。

items.example: Finitimus 'neighbouring' uses the same ending.
items.exampleCN: finitimus「毗邻的」使用同一词尾。

items.example: Maritimus was used of coasts and sea routes.
items.exampleCN: maritimus 曾用于海岸与海上路线。

items.example: Maritime trade shaped the port.
items.exampleCN: 海上贸易塑造了这座港口。

items.meaning: of the sea; a soldier serving at sea
items.meaningCN: 海洋的；在海上服役的士兵
items.example: Marine algae produce much of the world's oxygen.
items.exampleCN: 海洋藻类产生了世界上很大一部分氧气。

items.example: The old mariner knew the strait by heart.
items.exampleCN: 这位老水手对那条海峡了如指掌。

items.meaning: under the sea; a vessel that travels under water
items.meaningCN: 海面下的；在水下航行的舰艇
items.example: The submarine surfaced north of the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 潜艇在大陆架以北浮出水面。

items.meaning: a blue pigment once brought from beyond the sea
items.meaningCN: 一种最初从海外运来的蓝色颜料
items.example: The painter ground ultramarine for the sky.
items.exampleCN: 画家研磨群青来画天空。

items.meaningCN: 加拿大沿大西洋的诸省
items.example: Fishing still anchors the Maritimes.
items.exampleCN: 渔业仍是沿海诸省的支柱。

marinus, marina, marinum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_en: the salt water that makes up the sea, as opposed to fresh water on land
core_image: 一只从海边取回的样本瓶，瓶里是略带浑浊的咸水，瓶壁上已经结出细小的盐痕
scene: 实验台前，研究员举起刚取回的样本瓶说，This seawater has been filtered but not yet desalted.
sceneCN: 这里 seawater 指「从海里取来的咸水」（第 1 个义项：海洋中天然存在的咸水）；句意为：这份海水已经过滤，但还没有脱盐。

pos.zh: 海水；海洋咸水
海水制成的；使用海水的（如海水淡化、海水腐蚀）

forms.label: 复数（指不同水样或类型，罕用）

derivatives.zh: 海水入侵（沿海含水层被咸水侵入）
海水淡化
海水腐蚀

senses.title: The salt water of the sea
senses.titleCN: 海洋中天然存在的咸水
senses.definition: the natural salt water that fills the sea, taken as one substance rather than as a particular location
senses.definitionCN: 充满海洋的天然咸水，被当作一种物质而非某个具体地点
senses.example: This seawater has been filtered but not yet desalted.
senses.exampleCN: 这份海水已经过滤，但还没有脱盐。
senses.why: the compound simply names what the sea is made of, joining the place word to the substance word so that the material can be discussed on its own.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词只是说出海由什么构成，把地点词与物质词连在一起，好让这种材料能被单独讨论。

senses.title: Water taken as a usable resource
senses.titleCN: 作为可利用资源的海水
senses.definition: sea water regarded as a supply that can be treated and put to use, especially for drinking water
senses.definitionCN: 把海水视为可经处理后使用的供应来源，尤其用于制取饮用水
senses.example: The plant turns seawater into drinking water for the town.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂把海水变成供全镇饮用的水。
senses.why: dry coasts have water everywhere and none of it drinkable, so the same substance becomes a resource the moment a treatment plant stands beside it.
senses.whyCN: 干旱的海岸到处是水却没有一滴能喝，因此只要旁边立起一座处理厂，同一种物质就变成了资源。

senses.title: A chemical solution of salts
senses.definition: sea water studied as a solution of sodium, chloride, magnesium and other ions
senses.definitionCN: 把海水当作含钠、氯、镁等离子的溶液来研究
senses.example: Chemists measure the seawater's chloride content to estimate salinity.
senses.exampleCN: 化学家测定海水中的氯含量来估算盐度。
senses.why: once the water is filtered away conceptually, what remains is a list of dissolved ions, and that list is what ocean chemistry works with.
senses.whyCN: 一旦在概念上把水滤掉，剩下的就是一串溶解离子，而海洋化学处理的正是这张清单。

senses.title: Water for marine farming
senses.definition: sea water supplied to tanks or ponds to raise fish, shellfish and algae
senses.definitionCN: 供给水池或池塘，用来养鱼、贝类与藻类的海水
senses.example: The hatchery pumps seawater through the tanks all night.
senses.exampleCN: 孵化场整夜把海水泵入水槽。
senses.why: farming at sea means bringing the sea on land, so the word stops naming an open place and starts naming an input that must be pumped and filtered.
senses.whyCN: 在海上养殖等于把海搬到陆地，于是这个词不再指开阔地点，而指一种必须泵送、过滤的投入品。

senses.title: Water used in industry
senses.definition: sea water used for cooling, washing or ballast, and the corrosion problems it brings
senses.definitionCN: 用于冷却、冲洗或压载的海水，以及它带来的腐蚀问题
senses.example: Cheap seawater cooling saves energy but eats away at the pipes.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的海水冷却节省能源，却会腐蚀管道。
senses.why: industry wants a cold, plentiful liquid and the sea is the cheapest source; the salt that makes it useless for drinking makes it hard on metal, and both facts belong to this sense.
senses.whyCN: 工业需要又冷又多的液体，海是最便宜的来源；使它不能饮用的盐也使它侵蚀金属，这两个事实都属于这个义项。

senses.title: The boundary against fresh water
senses.titleCN: 与淡水相对的水体类型
senses.definition: the salt-water side of the division between marine and freshwater environments
senses.definitionCN: 海洋环境与淡水环境之分中属于咸水的那一侧
senses.example: Where seawater meets the river mouth, the two waters mix slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 海水与河口的相接处，两种水缓慢混合。
senses.why: ecology needs two labels for two chemistries, and seawater is the label for the salty side of that line, wherever the line happens to run.
senses.whyCN: 生态学需要为两种水化学各设一个标签，seawater 就是这条分界线上咸水一侧的标签，无论界线画在哪里。

senses.title: Seawater pushing into coastal ground
senses.definition: sea water that moves inland into coastal aquifers when fresh groundwater is overused
senses.definitionCN: 淡水地下水被过度抽取时，向内陆推进到沿海含水层的海水
senses.example: Heavy pumping let seawater reach the village wells.
senses.exampleCN: 过度抽水让海水侵入了村里的水井。
senses.why: fresh water floats on salt water at the coast in a delicate balance; take too much fresh water and the sea moves in, which is why the word appears in water-management reports.
senses.whyCN: 在海岸，淡水以微妙的平衡浮在咸水之上；淡水取多了，海就推进来，因此这个词出现在水资源管理报告中。

senses.title: A source of salinity-gradient energy
senses.definition: sea water used as one half of a salinity gradient that can generate electricity
senses.definitionCN: 作为盐度差的一半，用来发电的海水
senses.example: Engineers pair seawater with river water to test a new salinity battery.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师把海水与河水配对，测试一种新的盐差电池。
senses.why: the energy is not in the water as such but in the difference between salt and fresh, so seawater becomes one terminal of a chemical cell.
senses.whyCN: 能量并不在水本身，而在咸与淡之间的差异，因此海水成了化学电池的一端。

senses.title: The water as a habitat
senses.titleCN: 作为生物栖息水体的海水
senses.definition: the salt water considered as the medium in which marine organisms live, feed and reproduce
senses.definitionCN: 被视为海洋生物生存、摄食与繁殖介质的海水
senses.example: Warm seawater carries the larvae toward the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖的海水把幼体带向珊瑚礁。
senses.why: for a biologist the water is not empty space but a medium with temperature, oxygen and food in it, so the word names the whole environment rather than the liquid alone.
senses.whyCN: 在生物学家看来，水不是空无一物的空间，而是含温度、氧气与食物的介质，因此这个词命名的是整个环境，而不只是液体。

intro.en: Seawater is a native English compound of sea and water; both halves are Old English words, and the written form as one word is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: seawater 是英语本族复合词，由 sea 与 water 组成；两半都是古英语词，写成一个词的拼法属于现代用法。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English sæ meant 'sea, lake, large water' and is the source of modern sea; it is not related to the verb see 'to look'.
items.cn: 古英语 sæ 意为「海、湖、大片水域」，是现代 sea 的来源；它与动词 see「看见」没有词源关系。

items.en: Old English wæter is the common word for water and has stayed almost unchanged in form for a thousand years.
items.cn: 古英语 wæter 是「水」的常用词，一千年来词形几乎未变。

items.en: English often joins a place noun to a substance noun, as in seawater, rainwater and groundwater; the first element names the source, the second the material.
items.cn: 英语常把地点名词与物质名词连起来，如海水、雨水、地下水；前一成分说明来源，后一成分说明材料。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the solid spelling seawater spread in chemistry, engineering and navigation, where the substance had to be named precisely and repeatedly.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，连写形式 seawater 在化学、工程与航海写作中普及，因为这些领域需要精确而反复地命名这种物质。

items.en: Today seawater names the raw material of desalination, aquaculture, cooling systems, intrusion studies and salinity-gradient power, while the two-word sea water survives in general writing.
items.cn: 今天 seawater 指淡化、养殖、冷却系统、海水入侵研究与盐差发电的原料，而分写的 sea water 仍见于一般写作。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only, not root): the exact first written record of the compound is not fixed, because early texts vary between sea water and seawater; the deeper Indo-European forms behind both halves are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代，不涉及词根）：这个复合词最早的书证没有确切年代，因为早期文本在分写与连写之间摇摆；两半背后更早的印欧语形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds sea- compounds that share a first element but name something else; group two holds words for salty water that differ in strength or setting.
note.cn: 第一组是共享前一成分、却指别的事物的 sea- 复合词；第二组是都指咸水、但浓度或使用场景不同的词。

entries.definition: sea plus worthy: fit to sail safely, said of a boat rather than of water.
entries.definitionCN: sea 加 worthy：适航的、能安全航行的，说的是船而不是水。

entries.definition: sea plus -ward: turned or directed toward the sea, a direction rather than a substance.
entries.definitionCN: sea 加 -ward：朝向海的，表示方向而非物质。

entries.definition: sea plus wall: a barrier built to hold back the sea, so it names a construction, not the water.
entries.definitionCN: sea 加 wall：用来挡住海水的堤墙，因此指建筑而非海水。

entries.definition: sea plus bed: the floor beneath the sea, a place rather than the water in it.
entries.definitionCN: sea 加 bed：海面之下的底部，是地点而非其中的水。

entries.definition: the common compound salt plus water; it says what the water contains instead of where it comes from, and is the usual word in fishing and aquariums.
entries.definitionCN: 常用复合词 salt 加 water；它说明水含什么，而非水从哪里来，是捕鱼与水族领域的常用说法。

entries.definition: water with a very high salt content, far saltier than the open sea; it is what remains after desalination or what fills a salt works.
entries.definitionCN: 含盐量极高的水，远比外海咸；它是淡化后剩下的浓液，或盐场中的卤水。

entries.definition: a laboratory term for water containing dissolved salts at any strength, including brackish and sea water.
entries.definitionCN: 实验室术语，指含任何浓度溶解盐的水，包括半咸水与海水。

entries.definition: water identified by its location in the open ocean rather than by its salt content; it overlaps with seawater but points at the place.
entries.definitionCN: 按位于开阔大洋这一地点来指认的水，而非按含盐量；与 seawater 重叠，但指向地点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The compound is transparent: sea names the source, water names the material.
normal.cn: 这个复合词一目了然：sea 说明来源，water 说明材料。

normal.en: Old English sæ 'sea' and wæter 'water' are both native words, so nothing here is borrowed.
normal.cn: 古英语 sæ「海」与 wæter「水」都是本族词，这个词里没有借贷成分。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical senses: seawater desalination, seawater intrusion, seawater corrosion.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：海水淡化、海水入侵、海水腐蚀。

normal.en: The pair saltwater and freshwater marks the two chemical sides of the same division.
normal.cn: saltwater 与 freshwater 这一对词标出同一条分界的两侧。

normal.en: Ocean chemistry measures chloride first, because chloride is the most abundant ion in seawater.
normal.cn: 海洋化学先测氯，因为氯是海水中含量最高的离子。

abstract.en: Picture a glass of the sea that cannot be drunk, held right beside a tap that can.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯不能喝的海水，就放在一只可以喝的水龙头旁边。

abstract.en: Picture salt left on a window after the water has gone, drawing the shape of where it was.
abstract.cn: 想象水退去后留在窗上的盐痕，勾出它曾经所在的位置。

abstract.en: Picture two waters meeting at a river mouth and refusing to mix at once.
abstract.cn: 想象两条水在河口相遇，却不肯立刻混在一起。

examples.en: Desalination plants draw seawater and return the leftover brine to the sea.
examples.cn: 淡化厂抽取海水，再把剩下的浓盐水送回海里。

examples.en: Rising seas push seawater farther into the coastal aquifer each year.
examples.cn: 海平面上升使海水每年更深地侵入沿海含水层。

examples.en: The reef fish spawn in warm shallow seawater.
examples.cn: 礁鱼在温暖的浅海水中产卵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「稀窝头」——海边捡起的窝头被咸水泡过 → 海水、咸水

root: 英语本族复合词：sea（古英语 sæ「海、湖」）+ water（古英语 wæter「水」）；两部分的更早印欧形式均为重构，词根无存疑，仅复合词首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one substance through different hands: the sea's own water, a supply to be treated, a chemical solution, a farming input, an industrial coolant, the salty side of a boundary, an intruder underground, a battery terminal, and finally a habitat.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项让同一种物质经过不同人的手：海自己的水、待处理的供应、化学溶液、养殖投入、工业冷却剂、分界的咸水一侧、地下的入侵者、电池的一端，最后是生物栖息的环境。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sample bottle of salty water with salt already tracing the glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只装着咸水的样本瓶，盐已经在瓶壁上留下痕迹。

branches.en: WHAT IT IS: the substance is defined by its salts, and that definition draws the line against fresh water.
branches.cn: 它是什么：这种物质由盐分定义，而这一界定也划出了与淡水的界线。

branches.en: WHAT IT CAN GIVE: the same water becomes drinking water in a plant and electricity in a salinity cell.
branches.cn: 它能给出什么：同一片水在工厂里变成饮用水，在盐差电池里变成电。

branches.en: INSIDE THE WATER: chemistry sees dissolved ions, biology sees a medium full of life.
branches.cn: 水里面：化学看见溶解的离子，生物学看见充满生命的介质。

branches.en: PUT TO WORK: ponds pump it in to raise shellfish, plants pump it in to cool pipes.
branches.cn: 拿来使用：池塘泵入它养贝，工厂泵入它冷却管道。

branches.en: WHEN IT MOVES INLAND: over-pumping fresh groundwater lets the sea reach wells that were once sweet.
branches.cn: 当它向内陆推进：过度抽取淡水，海就抵达了原本甘甜的水井。

intro.en: Seawater is a native compound, so its analysis is simpler than a Latin word: two Old English nouns, plus a family of sea- compounds built on the same first element.
intro.cn: seawater 是本族复合词，分析起来比拉丁词简单：两个古英语名词，再加一族共享同一前成分的 sea- 复合词。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin root; Latin would express the idea with aqua marina, a phrase rather than a cognate, so latinEntries is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根；拉丁语会用 aqua marina 这一短语表达同一概念，那是短语而非同族词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.meaning: the salt water, or a large lake
items.example: Old English sæ could name a lake as well as the sea.
items.exampleCN: 古英语 sæ 既可指海，也可指湖。

items.example: Wæter is one of the oldest unchanged nouns in English.
items.exampleCN: wæter 是英语中词形最久未变的名词之一。

items.example: The tank holds filtered seawater.
items.exampleCN: 这个水槽装着过滤过的海水。

items.example: Saltwater kills most garden plants.
items.exampleCN: 咸水会杀死大多数园林植物。

items.example: Freshwater fish cannot survive in the bay.
items.exampleCN: 淡水鱼无法在海湾中存活。

items.meaning: salt water pushing into coastal groundwater
items.example: Seawater intrusion salted three village wells.
items.exampleCN: 海水入侵使三口村井变咸。

items.example: The bridge uses seawater-resistant steel.
items.exampleCN: 这座桥使用耐海水钢材。

items.example: Seawater desalination supplies the dry coast.
items.exampleCN: 海水淡化为干旱的海岸供水。

items.meaning: a wall built against the sea
items.example: The seawall held through the storm.
items.exampleCN: 海堤在风暴中撑住了。

definition_en: the amount of dissolved salt contained in water or soil, usually measured in parts per thousand
core_image: 一支比重计插进水样，刻度停在一个数上，数值越高，水就越咸
scene: 海洋调查船上，技术员把探头放进一桶刚打上来的水说，The salinity here is high enough to float an egg.
sceneCN: 这里 salinity 指「水中溶解盐的含量」（第 1 个义项：以千分比表示的含盐量）；句意为：这里的盐度高到能让鸡蛋浮起来。

pos.zh: 盐度；含盐量；（土壤）盐渍化程度

derivatives.zh: 含盐的；咸的 / 盐水
盐渍化；盐化过程
使盐化；使含盐
脱盐；海水淡化
盐度计；盐量计

senses.title: The amount of salt dissolved in water
senses.definition: the quantity of dissolved salts in water, considered as a measurable property of the water
senses.definitionCN: 水中溶解盐的数量，被视为水的一项可测属性
senses.example: The salinity here is high enough to float an egg.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的盐度高到能让鸡蛋浮起来。
senses.why: Latin sal 'salt' plus the adjective suffix -inus and the noun suffix -ity produce a word that names a quality, so salinity is salt-ness measured rather than salt itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 sal「盐」加形容词后缀 -inus 与名词后缀 -ity，造出一个指性质的名词，因此 salinity 是可被测量的「咸的程度」，而不是盐本身。

senses.title: The oceanographic measurement
senses.titleCN: 海洋学中的盐度计量值
senses.definition: the standard measure of sea water's salt content, reported in parts per thousand or on the practical salinity scale
senses.definitionCN: 海水含盐量的标准量值，以千分比或实用盐度标度表示
senses.example: Surface salinity falls sharply where the river empties into the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 河水注入海湾处，表层盐度急剧下降。
senses.why: a property that varies from place to place needs a scale, and oceanography fixed one so that a number on a chart means the same thing on every ship.
senses.whyCN: 一项随地点变化的属性需要一个标度，海洋学因此固定了一套，使海图上的一个数字在每条船上都表示同一件事。

senses.title: Salt accumulated in soil
senses.definition: the concentration of salts left in soil, often after irrigation water evaporates
senses.definitionCN: 留在土壤中的盐分浓度，常由灌溉水蒸发后形成
senses.example: Years of flood irrigation raised the salinity of the field.
senses.exampleCN: 多年大水漫灌提高了这块田的盐度。
senses.why: water brought to a dry field carries a little salt, and when the water leaves by evaporation the salt stays; repeat that and the soil itself becomes the container.
senses.whyCN: 引到旱地的水带着少量盐，水蒸发离开后盐却留下；如此反复，土壤本身就成了盛盐的容器。

senses.title: The gradient in an estuary
senses.definition: the gradual change from fresh river water to salt sea water across an estuary
senses.definitionCN: 河口处从淡水到海水逐渐变化的盐度过渡
senses.example: Oysters cluster where the salinity stays between fresh and full sea.
senses.exampleCN: 牡蛎聚集在盐度介于淡水与全海水之间的地带。
senses.why: two waters meet without mixing at once, so salinity becomes a map of distance from the river mouth rather than a single number.
senses.whyCN: 两种水相遇却不会立刻混匀，因此盐度成了一张标示离河口远近的地图，而不是一个孤立的数字。

senses.title: The limit an organism can bear
senses.titleCN: 生物所能承受的盐度上限
senses.definition: the range of salt concentration within which a plant or animal can survive
senses.definitionCN: 某种动植物能够存活的含盐浓度范围
senses.example: Few crops have enough salinity tolerance for that coastal soil.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有作物对那片沿海土壤具有足够的耐盐性。
senses.why: for a living thing the number stops being chemistry and becomes a threshold: above it, water is pulled out of the cells and the organism fails.
senses.whyCN: 对生物而言，这个数字不再是化学，而是阈值：超过它，水被从细胞中抽走，生物便无法存活。

senses.title: The difference used to make power
senses.definition: the difference in salt concentration between two waters, exploited to drive turbines or cells
senses.definitionCN: 两种水之间含盐浓度的差异，被用来驱动涡轮或电池
senses.example: The pilot plant runs on the salinity difference between river and sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这座试验电厂靠河水与海水的盐度差运转。
senses.why: mixing salt and fresh water releases energy that was stored in the separation, so the measurement itself becomes a fuel gauge.
senses.whyCN: 咸淡水混合会释放储存在分离状态中的能量，因此这个量值本身就成了燃料表。

senses.title: Salt strength in food and brine
senses.definition: the salt concentration of a brine, sauce or preserved food, judged by taste or by recipe
senses.definitionCN: 卤水、酱汁或腌制品中的盐浓度，按口味或配方判断
senses.example: The cheesemaker checks the brine's salinity before soaking the curds.
senses.exampleCN: 奶酪师在浸泡凝乳前先检查卤水的咸度。
senses.why: the kitchen uses the same idea at a smaller scale: brine is sea water made on purpose, and its salinity decides how much water leaves the food.
senses.whyCN: 厨房以更小的尺度使用同一观念：卤水是人工配制的海水，其盐度决定有多少水从食物中被抽出。

senses.title: A water-quality limit for irrigation
senses.titleCN: 灌溉水质中的盐度限值
senses.definition: the salt level of irrigation water above which crops or pipes are harmed
senses.definitionCN: 灌溉水含盐量超过即会损害作物或管道的水平
senses.example: The agency sets a salinity limit for water released into farmland.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构为排入农田的水设定了盐度限值。
senses.why: once water is managed, the property becomes a rule on paper: a threshold that decides whether a river may be used on a field.
senses.whyCN: 一旦水被管理，这项属性就变成纸面上的规则：一个决定河水能否用于农田的阈值。

senses.title: A clue to past climate
senses.definition: an ancient salt level read from sediments or ice, used to reconstruct past ocean and climate conditions
senses.definitionCN: 从沉积物或冰芯中读出的古代含盐量，用来重建过去的海洋与气候状况
senses.example: The core's salinity record shows a sudden shift in rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 岩芯的盐度记录显示降雨曾突然改变。
senses.why: salt leaves a chemical trace in mud and ice, so a value measured today can stand for a sea that disappeared long ago.
senses.whyCN: 盐在泥沙与冰中留下化学痕迹，因此今天测得的数值可以代表一片早已消失的海。

intro.en: Salinity is a Latin-based noun: sal 'salt' produced the adjective salinus 'of salt', and English added -ity to name the quality. The modern scientific sense developed in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: salinity 是拉丁系名词：sal「盐」构成形容词 salinus「盐的」，英语再加 -ity 命名这一性质；现代科学义到 19 世纪才发展起来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sal, salis is the Latin noun for salt; it is the base of a large family including salinus, salarium and the verb salire 'to salt'.
items.cn: Sal, salis 是拉丁语中指盐的名词；它是 salinus、salarium 以及动词 salire「加盐」等一大批词的基干。

items.en: Salinus 'of salt, salty' adds -inus to sal; English saline comes directly from this adjective.
items.cn: salinus「盐的、咸的」在 sal 后加 -inus；英语 saline 直接来自这个形容词。

items.en: The Latin noun suffix -itas (English -ity) turns an adjective into a name for a quality, which is the pattern behind salinity, clarity and humidity.
items.cn: 拉丁名词后缀 -itas（英语作 -ity）把形容词变成指性质的名词，salinity、clarity、humidity 都循这一模式。

items.en: English salinity is recorded from the nineteenth century, when chemistry and oceanography needed a technical noun distinct from the everyday word saltiness.
items.cn: 英语 salinity 的书证见于 19 世纪，当时化学与海洋学需要一个区别于日常词 saltiness 的技术名词。

items.en: In the twentieth century salinity was tied to electrical conductivity and later to a practical scale, so that a measured number could be compared across oceans and decades.
items.cn: 20 世纪，盐度与电导率挂钩，后来又绑定到一套实用标度，使测得的数值可以跨大洋、跨年代比较。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only, not root): the earliest English citation is not precisely fixed, and the exact route through French salinité is generally accepted but not documented step by step; the Indo-European form *sal- behind Latin sal is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代，不涉及词根）：英语最早书证没有确切年份；经法语 salinité 传入的路径属于「一般认为是」，但缺少逐步文献；拉丁 sal 背后的印欧形式 *sal- 是重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like salinity but do not all share the salt root; group two holds measures and qualities of salt water.
note.cn: 第一组是与 salinity 形近、但并非都同出盐词根的词；第二组是海水含盐量的相关说法。

entries.definition: the adjective from Latin salinus, meaning containing salt; salinity is the noun built from it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 salinus 的形容词，意为含盐的；salinity 是由它构成的名词。

entries.definition: the process by which soil or water becomes salty; it names the change, while salinity names the amount.
entries.definitionCN: 土壤或水变咸的过程；它指变化，而 salinity 指数量。

entries.definition: from Latin sanus 'healthy': soundness of mind. It looks close to salinity but has no salt in it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 sanus「健康的」：神志健全。它与 salinity 形近，却与盐毫无关系。

entries.definition: salt-bearing, from sal plus -ferous 'carrying'; it describes rock or springs, not a measured amount.
entries.definitionCN: 含盐的，由 sal 加 -ferous「携带」构成；它描写岩石或泉，而不是一个测得的量。

entries.definition: the plain English word for how salty something tastes; salinity is its scientific counterpart for water and soil.
entries.definitionCN: 指尝起来有多咸的日常英语词；salinity 是它在水与土壤领域的技术对应词。

entries.definition: the quality of being slightly salty, as in an estuary; it covers only the middle of the salinity range.
entries.definitionCN: 指略带咸味的性质，如河口；它只覆盖盐度范围的中间段。

entries.definition: the mass of chloride in sea water, historically used to calculate salinity; it measures one ion, not all salts.
entries.definitionCN: 海水中氯的质量，历史上用来推算盐度；它测的是一种离子，而非全部盐类。

entries.definition: the mass of all dissolved material in water, of which salt is only a part; the term is broader than salinity.
entries.definitionCN: 水中全部溶解物质的质量，盐只是其中一部分；这个术语比 salinity 更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin sal 'salt' plus -inus plus -ity: salt-ness turned into a measurable noun.
normal.cn: 拉丁 sal「盐」加 -inus 再加 -ity：把「咸」变成可测量的名词。

normal.en: The family runs saline, salinity, salinization, salinize, desalination, salimeter.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 saline、salinity、salinization、salinize、desalination、salimeter。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical sense: surface salinity, soil salinity, salinity gradient, salinity tolerance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出技术义：表层盐度、土壤盐度、盐度梯度、耐盐性。

normal.en: The everyday word is saltiness; salinity is what a laboratory reports.
normal.cn: 日常说法是 saltiness；salinity 是实验室报告里的用词。

normal.en: Oceanographers often report salinity in parts per thousand, written with the per-mille sign.
normal.cn: 海洋学家常以千分比报告盐度，写作千分号。

abstract.en: Picture a float that sits higher in the glass the saltier the water becomes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只浮子，水越咸，它在杯中就浮得越高。

abstract.en: Picture a field that turns white after the irrigation water dries.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田在灌溉水干后泛出白色。

abstract.en: Picture a river and a sea meeting but keeping their separate colours for a while.
abstract.cn: 想象河与海相遇，却在一段时间里各自保留颜色。

examples.en: Melting ice lowers the salinity of the surface water around it.
examples.cn: 融冰会降低其周围表层水的盐度。

examples.en: Irrigation without drainage slowly raises soil salinity.
examples.cn: 只灌不排会慢慢提高土壤盐度。

examples.en: The instrument logs salinity every ten metres of depth.
examples.cn: 仪器每下潜十米记录一次盐度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒了盐」——水里撒了盐，咸度就上去了 → 盐度、含盐量

root: 拉丁 sal「盐」→ salinus「盐的、咸的」+ 名词后缀 -itas/-ity → 英语 salinity；同根另有 saline、salarium（盐钱→薪水）、desalination。拉丁 sal 的印欧来源 *sal- 为重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one number as it changes hands: a property of water, a scale on a chart, a crust in a field, a gradient in an estuary, a survival limit, a fuel, a brine recipe, a legal threshold, and a trace of ancient rain.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟着同一个数值换手：水的属性、海图上的标度、田里的盐壳、河口的梯度、生存的上限、燃料、卤水配方、法定阈值，以及古代降雨的痕迹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hydrometer standing in a sample, its scale marking how salty the water is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支比重计立在水样中，刻度标出这水有多咸。

branches.en: WHAT IS COUNTED: the quality itself, then the scale that lets one ship's number be compared with another's.
branches.cn: 数的是什么：先是性质本身，然后是让一条船的数字能与另一条船比较的标度。

branches.en: ON LAND: evaporation leaves salt in the field, and managers turn the measure into a legal limit.
branches.cn: 在陆地上：蒸发把盐留在田里，管理者再把这一量值变成法定限值。

branches.en: ACROSS SPACE AND TIME: a gradient maps the estuary, and a sediment core maps ancient rainfall.
branches.cn: 跨空间与时间：梯度绘出河口，沉积岩芯绘出古代降雨。

branches.en: AT THE THRESHOLD: too much salt stops a crop, and the right amount preserves a cheese.
branches.cn: 在阈值上：盐太多作物就活不了，盐适量则能腌好奶酪。

branches.en: AS FUEL: the difference between salt and fresh water can be spent as electricity.
branches.cn: 当作燃料：咸水与淡水之间的差异可以当作电来花。

intro.en: Salinity is built from a Latin root and two suffixes, and the same pieces recur across chemistry and water science.
intro.cn: salinity 由一个拉丁词根与两个后缀构成，这些构件在化学与水科学中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin sal gives salinus, salarium and salinitas-like formations; the -ity suffix is the English reflex of Latin -itas.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sal 衍生 salinus、salarium 以及类似 salinitas 的构词；-ity 后缀是拉丁 -itas 在英语中的对应形式。

senses.title: Containing dissolved salt
senses.definition: containing salt dissolved in water, as a chemical property rather than a taste
senses.definitionCN: 水中溶有盐，指化学性质而非口味
senses.example: The saline groundwater lies just below the field.
senses.exampleCN: 含盐地下水就位于这块田的下方。
senses.why: Latin salinus 'of salt' adds -inus to sal 'salt', so the adjective simply marks the presence of salt in whatever it describes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 salinus「盐的」在 sal「盐」后加 -inus，因此这个形容词只是标记所描写之物含有盐。

senses.title: Tasting of salt
senses.definition: having a salty taste, said of food, drink or tears
senses.definitionCN: 带有咸味，用于食物、饮料或眼泪
senses.example: A saline tang came from the oysters, not the sauce.
senses.exampleCN: 那股咸味来自牡蛎，而不是酱汁。
senses.why: the tongue is a crude chemical detector, so the same adjective that marks dissolved salt in a lab also describes the sensation salt produces.
senses.whyCN: 舌头是一台粗略的化学探测器，因此实验室里标记溶解盐的同一个形容词，也用来描写盐带来的感觉。

senses.title: A prepared salt solution
senses.definition: water with a controlled amount of salt added, made for a specific purpose
senses.definitionCN: 按特定用途加入定量盐分的水
senses.example: Mix a saline solution to clean the wound.
senses.exampleCN: 配一份盐水溶液来清洗伤口。
senses.why: once salt is added by measure rather than found in nature, the adjective shifts from a description to a recipe.
senses.whyCN: 当盐是按量加入而非天然存在时，这个形容词就从描述变成了配方。

senses.title: The medical drip
senses.definition: a bag of salt water at body strength, given through a vein to restore fluid
senses.definitionCN: 一袋浓度与体液相近的盐水，经静脉输入以补充液体
senses.example: The nurse replaced the saline drip before the operation.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在手术前更换了生理盐水输液。
senses.why: blood is itself saline, so a solution matched to it can enter a vein without upsetting the cells; the noun shortens the full phrase.
senses.whyCN: 血液本身就是含盐的，因此浓度与之匹配的溶液能进入静脉而不扰乱细胞；名词形式是完整短语的省略。

senses.title: Salt-affected soil
senses.definition: soil in which salts have accumulated until most crops struggle
senses.definitionCN: 盐分积聚到多数作物难以生长的土壤
senses.example: Willows are among the few trees that tolerate saline soil.
senses.exampleCN: 柳树是少数能耐盐渍土的树木之一。
senses.why: the adjective attaches to the ground when irrigation or a rising water table leaves salt behind, turning a water problem into a land problem.
senses.whyCN: 当灌溉或地下水位上升把盐留下时，这个形容词就附着到土地上，把水的问题变成了地的问题。

senses.title: A salt lake
senses.definition: a lake with no outlet whose water has become far saltier than the sea
senses.definitionCN: 没有出水口、水比海咸得多的湖泊
senses.example: Nothing but algae grows in that saline lake.
senses.exampleCN: 那座盐湖里只长藻类。
senses.why: a lake that only loses water by evaporation keeps every grain of salt it receives, so the adjective marks the end point of that process.
senses.whyCN: 只靠蒸发失水的湖泊会把收到的每一粒盐都留下，因此这个形容词标记的正是这一过程的终点。

senses.title: A nasal rinse
senses.definition: a mild salt solution used to flush the nose and sinuses
senses.definitionCN: 用来冲洗鼻腔与鼻窦的淡盐水
senses.example: A warm saline rinse eased the congestion.
senses.exampleCN: 温盐水冲洗缓解了鼻塞。
senses.why: the nose lining is sensitive to concentration, so a solution close to body salt can clean it without stinging, and the adjective guarantees that strength.
senses.whyCN: 鼻黏膜对浓度敏感，接近体液盐度的溶液能清洁而不刺痛，这个形容词保证的正是这一浓度。

senses.title: An eyewash or lens rinse
senses.titleCN: 洗眼或镜片冲洗用的盐水
senses.definition: a sterile salt solution used to rinse the eye or a contact lens
senses.definitionCN: 用来冲洗眼睛或隐形眼镜的无菌盐水
senses.example: Rinse the lens in saline, never in tap water.
senses.exampleCN: 用盐水冲洗镜片，绝不要用自来水。
senses.why: tap water carries microbes and the wrong concentration, so a prepared saline keeps the eye at its own chemistry.
senses.whyCN: 自来水带有微生物且浓度不对，因此配制好的盐水能让眼睛保持自身的化学环境。

senses.title: Salt stress in plants
senses.definition: describing conditions in which too much salt in water or soil harms plants
senses.definitionCN: 水或土壤中盐分过多而伤害植物的状况
senses.example: Saline irrigation reduced the yield by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 含盐灌溉使产量减少了三分之一。
senses.why: salt outside the root pulls water out of it by osmosis, so an adjective about chemistry becomes a word about drought inside a living plant.
senses.whyCN: 根外的盐通过渗透把水从根中抽出，因此一个化学形容词变成了描述植物体内干旱的词。

intro.en: Saline comes from Latin salinus 'of salt', an adjective from sal 'salt'. English borrowed it in the seventeenth century, and the medical noun followed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: saline 来自拉丁 salinus「盐的」，由 sal「盐」构成的形容词；英语在 17 世纪借入，医用名词随后出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sal 'salt' is a third-declension noun whose compounds and derivatives spread across medicine, cooking and trade.
items.cn: sal「盐」是第三变格名词，其复合词与派生词遍及医学、烹饪与贸易。

items.en: Salinus 'of salt, salty' adds -inus to the noun; the same suffix builds other quality adjectives such as marinus from mare.
items.cn: salinus「盐的、咸的」在名词后加 -inus；同一后缀也构成 marinus（由 mare「海」）等其他性质形容词。

items.en: The plural salinae named salt works and salt pans, the places where sea water was evaporated for salt.
items.cn: 复数 salinae 指盐场与盐田，即蒸发海水取盐的地方。

items.en: English took the adjective in the seventeenth century through French salin, first describing springs, wells and mineral waters.
items.cn: 英语在 17 世纪经法语 salin 借入这个形容词，最初用于描写泉、井与矿泉水。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the noun saline settled into medicine for a salt solution matched to body fluids, and later for the drip that carries it.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，名词 saline 在医学中固定指与体液匹配的盐溶液，后来又指输送它的输液。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only, not root): the earliest English citation is not firmly dated, and whether the noun entered directly from Latin or through French is generally accepted rather than proved; the Indo-European *sal- behind sal is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代，不涉及词根）：英语最早书证年代不确，名词是直接来自拉丁还是经法语传入属「一般认为是」，尚未证实；sal 背后的印欧 *sal- 为重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words built on or resembling the salt stem; group two holds words for salty water at different strengths.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在盐词干上或与之形近的词；第二组是不同浓度的咸水说法。

entries.definition: the measured amount of salt in water; saline is the adjective and salinity the quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 水中盐的测得含量；saline 是形容词，salinity 是数量。

entries.definition: a salt lake, salt pan or salt works, from Latin salinae; it names a place, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 盐湖、盐田或盐场，来自拉丁 salinae；它指地点，不指性质。

entries.definition: from Latin sanus 'healthy': soundness of mind. The shape is close, but there is no salt in the root.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 sanus「健康的」：神志健全。词形接近，但词根中没有盐。

entries.definition: the same word is also heard with stress on the second syllable in some medical speech; the spelling and meaning do not change.
entries.definitionCN: 在部分医学口语中，这个词也可把重音放在第二音节；拼写与词义不变。

entries.definition: the everyday adjective for a salty taste; saline is its technical and medical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指咸味的日常形容词；saline 是它在技术与医学语境中的对应词。

entries.definition: very salty, like brine; it often describes the sea or tears and sounds more literary than saline.
entries.definitionCN: 很咸的，如卤水；常描写海或眼泪，比 saline 更有文学色彩。

entries.definition: slightly salty because fresh and sea water have mixed; it is weaker than saline and tied to estuaries.
entries.definitionCN: 因淡水与海水混合而略带咸味；比 saline 弱，且与河口相关。

entries.definition: the substance itself, not a property; saline describes water that contains it.
entries.definitionCN: 指物质本身，而非性质；saline 描写含有这种物质的水。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin sal 'salt' plus -inus: the adjective simply says 'of salt'.
normal.cn: 拉丁 sal「盐」加 -inus：这个形容词只是说「盐的」。

normal.en: The family runs saline, salinity, salinization, salinize, desalination, salina.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 saline、salinity、salinization、salinize、desalination、salina。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the uses: saline solution, saline drip, saline soil, saline lake.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把用法分开：盐水溶液、生理盐水输液、盐渍土、盐湖。

normal.en: A saline drip is blood's chemistry imitated in a bag.
normal.cn: 生理盐水输液就是把血液的化学环境装进一个袋子。

normal.en: Salinae in Latin were salt works, which is why salina means a salt pan today.
normal.cn: 拉丁 salinae 是盐场，因此今天的 salina 指盐田。

abstract.en: Picture a tear that a chemist and a cook would describe with the same word.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴眼泪，化学家和厨师会用同一个词来描写它。

abstract.en: Picture a lake with no door, keeping every grain of salt it ever received.
abstract.cn: 想象一座没有出口的湖，把收到的每一粒盐都留下。

abstract.en: Picture a plant drinking from a glass it cannot reach without paying for it.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物从一只杯子里喝水，却要为每一口付出代价。

examples.en: The clinic keeps saline solution in every treatment room.
examples.cn: 诊所的每间治疗室都备有生理盐水。

examples.en: Saline lakes form where rivers bring salt in and only evaporation takes water out.
examples.cn: 河流带入盐分、而只有蒸发带走水的地方，会形成盐湖。

examples.en: Saline groundwater limits what can be planted along the coast.
examples.cn: 含盐地下水限制了沿海可以种植的作物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒来盐」——把盐撒进水里，就成了盐水 → 含盐的、生理盐水

root: 拉丁 sal「盐」+ 形容词后缀 -inus → salinus「盐的、咸的」→ 法语 salin → 英语 saline；名词 saline 到 19 世纪在医学中固定为生理盐水。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin with a chemical presence and then move through taste, a prepared solution, the drip in a ward, salt-crusted soil, a closed lake, a rinse for nose and eye, and the stress salt puts on a living plant.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从「含有盐」这一化学事实出发，随后经过味觉、配制溶液、病房里的输液、结盐的土壤、封闭的湖泊、鼻腔与眼睛的冲洗，最后是盐给活体植物带来的胁迫。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bag of clear salt water hanging by a hospital bed, matched to the salt of blood.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只透明的盐水袋挂在病床边，浓度与血液中的盐相匹配。

branches.en: CHEMICAL PRESENCE: the adjective marks dissolved salt before any use is imagined.
branches.cn: 化学上的存在：在设想任何用途之前，这个形容词先标记溶解的盐。

branches.en: THE TONGUE'S REPORT: the same presence becomes a sensation when tasted.
branches.cn: 舌头的报告：同一种存在被尝到时，变成一种感觉。

branches.en: MADE ON PURPOSE: solution, drip, nasal rinse and eyewash are all salt water prepared to a chosen strength for a body.
branches.cn: 刻意配制：溶液、输液、鼻腔冲洗与洗眼液，都是按选定浓度为身体配制的盐水。

branches.en: WHEN IT HARMS: salt left in soil and salt outside a root both take water away.
branches.cn: 当它造成伤害：留在土里的盐与根外的盐，都会把水夺走。

branches.en: WHERE IT COLLECTS: a lake with no outlet keeps every grain and turns into brine.
branches.cn: 它汇聚之处：没有出口的湖留下每一粒盐，最终变成卤水。

intro.en: Saline is a Latin adjective with a transparent suffix; the same root also builds the nouns and compounds of water science and medicine.
intro.cn: saline 是一个后缀清晰的拉丁形容词；同一词根还构成水科学与医学中的名词与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sal gives salinus and salinae; English saline comes from salinus, while salina and salinity follow the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sal 衍生 salinus 与 salinae；英语 saline 来自 salinus，salina 与 salinity 则循同一词干。

items.example: Sal was weighed and taxed like a precious good.
items.exampleCN: 盐曾像贵重货物一样被称量与征税。

items.example: Salinus and marinus share the same ending.
items.exampleCN: salinus 与 marinus 共享同一词尾。

items.example: A saline spring feeds the marsh.
items.exampleCN: 一眼盐泉供给这片沼泽。

items.example: The salina produces salt by evaporation.
items.exampleCN: 盐田靠蒸发制盐。

items.example: Salinity controls where oysters grow.
items.exampleCN: 盐度决定牡蛎生长的地方。

items.example: Salinization follows poor drainage.
items.exampleCN: 排水不良之后便是盐渍化。

items.example: Rising water salinizes the low fields.
items.exampleCN: 水位上升使低田盐化。

items.example: Desalination made the town habitable.
items.exampleCN: 淡化技术让这座城得以居住。

items.example: The salimeter was calibrated at sea.
items.exampleCN: 这台盐度计在海上校准过。

senses.title: Water that keeps moving in one direction
senses.titleCN: 朝一个方向持续流动的水
senses.definition: a body of water moving continuously in a particular direction, as in a river or the sea
senses.definitionCN: 在河流或海洋中沿特定方向持续流动的水体
senses.example: A strong current swept the boat downstream.
senses.exampleCN: 强劲的水流把船冲向下游。
senses.why: Latin currens is simply 'running', the present participle of currere 'to run'; water that runs is a current, and no further metaphor is needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 currens 就是「跑着的」，是 currere「跑」的现在分词；会跑的水就是水流，这里不需要再添比喻。

senses.title: Air moving as a stream
senses.definition: a mass of air moving steadily in a particular direction, especially one that can be felt or measured
senses.definitionCN: 沿特定方向稳定流动的一大团空气，尤指能被感觉到或测量到的
senses.example: A warm current of air rose from the valley floor.
senses.exampleCN: 一股暖空气从谷底升起。
senses.why: the participle does not care what substance runs; once air is treated as a fluid, the word for running water transfers to it unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 这个分词并不在意跑动的是什么物质；一旦把空气当作流体，指流水的那同一个词就原封不动地移用过来。

senses.title: Charge in motion
senses.definition: the flow of electric charge through a wire or other conductor
senses.definitionCN: 电荷在导线或其他导体中的流动
senses.example: The meter shows a current of two amperes.
senses.exampleCN: 电表显示电流为两安培。
senses.why: nineteenth-century physics needed a word for electricity that moves, and the everyday image of a running stream supplied it without a new coinage.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪的物理学需要一个词指会流动的电，日常「奔跑的水流」这一意象不必另造新词就提供了它。

senses.title: The drift of opinion or events
senses.definition: the general direction in which opinion, fashion or events are moving at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期舆论、风气或事件发展的总方向
senses.example: The current of public opinion turned against the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 舆论的走向转为反对该计划。
senses.why: a tendency is imagined as something that flows and carries people with it, so the word for moving water comes to name the direction of a debate.
senses.whyCN: 趋势被想象成会流动、会带着人走的东西，于是指流动之水的词被用来命名一场争论的方向。

senses.title: Happening now
senses.definition: existing or happening at the present time, as opposed to the past or the future
senses.definitionCN: 存在于或发生于现在，与过去或未来相对
senses.example: The current budget covers only this year.
senses.exampleCN: 当前预算只覆盖今年。
senses.why: from 'running' comes 'still running on': what is current is what has not stopped and has not ended, namely the present state of things.
senses.whyCN: 从「跑着的」引申出「仍在跑着」：current 就是尚未停下、尚未结束的东西，也就是事物的当下状态。

senses.title: Still in circulation
senses.definition: of money, words or practices: accepted and in use at the present time
senses.definitionCN: 指货币、词语或做法：当下被接受并仍在使用的
senses.example: That coin is no longer current.
senses.exampleCN: 那种硬币已不再流通。
senses.why: money and words circulate the way water runs; whatever still passes from hand to hand or mouth to mouth is literally still moving.
senses.whyCN: 货币与词语像水一样流通；仍在手与手之间、口与口之间传递的东西，字面上就是仍在运动的。

senses.title: In force
senses.definition: of a law, rule or version: officially valid at the present time
senses.definitionCN: 指法律、规章或版本：当下正式有效的
senses.example: Under the current rules, boats may not enter the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 按现行规定，船只不得进入该海湾。
senses.why: a rule that has not been repealed is still running through the institutions that apply it, so validity and motion share one adjective.
senses.whyCN: 未被废止的规则仍在执行它的机构里「跑着」，因此有效与运动共用同一个形容词。

senses.title: Holding the post now
senses.definition: of a person: holding a particular office or position at the present time
senses.definitionCN: 指人：当下担任某一职务或职位的
senses.example: The current chairman took office in March.
senses.exampleCN: 现任主席于三月就职。
senses.why: the person in office is the one whose term is running now, which is why the same word marks both the holder and the moment.
senses.whyCN: 在任者就是任期正在「跑」的那个人，因此同一个词既标人，也标时刻。

senses.title: Running, as an older descriptive word
senses.titleCN: 流动的、奔流的（书面旧用法）
senses.definition: flowing or running, used of water or another liquid in older and literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 流动的、奔流的，旧时与文学写作中用于水或其他液体
senses.example: A current stream ran under the wooden bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一条流动的溪水从木桥下流过。
senses.why: this is the participle's oldest layer, kept alive in poetry and description after the noun senses took over everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 这是分词最古老的一层意思，在各名词义项接管日常用法之后仍活在诗歌与描写文字里。

intro.en: Current comes from Latin currere 'to run' through its present participle currens, current-, and reached English by way of Old French corant. The sense 'water in motion' is centuries older than the electrical one. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: current 源自拉丁 currere「跑」的现在分词 currens, current-，经古法语 corant 进入英语；「流动的水」这一义项比电学义早了好几个世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Currere 'to run' is the verb at the base; the same stem also yields cursus 'a running, course', cursor 'runner' and the frequentative cursare.
items.cn: currere「跑」是位于底层的动词；同一词干还产生 cursus「奔跑、路线」、cursor「奔跑者」以及反复动词 cursare。

items.en: The present participle currens, current- means 'running'; Latin already used it as an adjective, and in some contexts as a noun for a stream of water.
items.cn: 现在分词 currens, current- 意为「跑着的」；拉丁语已把它用作形容词，在某些语境中也用作指水流的名词。

items.en: Old French corant, the ancestor of modern courant, passed the word into Middle English in the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries, where it first described water in motion.
items.cn: 古法语 corant（现代法语 courant 的前身）在 13、14 世纪把这个词传给中古英语，最初描写流动的水。

items.en: Seafarers spoke of currents in the sea by the sixteenth century, and the same word was soon applied to moving air; both keep the image of a stream that runs.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪航海者已用 current 指海中的水流，同一个词很快也用于流动的空气；两者都保留了「奔跑的溪流」这一意象。

items.en: When electricity became a measurable flowing quantity in the early nineteenth century, the old stream image was borrowed once more for charge in motion.
items.cn: 19 世纪初电成为可测量的流动量时，「溪流」这一旧意象再次被借去指运动中的电荷。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only, not first date): Latin currere is well documented, but its Indo-European source is reconstructed as *kers- 'to run' and remains a hypothesis; the earliest English uses of the adjective and the noun are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（指词根，不涉及首见年代）：拉丁 currere 文献确凿，但其印欧来源一般重构为 *kers-「跑」，仍是假说；该词形容词与名词用法在英语中的最早书证只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like current or grow from the same Latin stem; group two holds words for movement and direction that differ in what actually moves.
note.cn: 第一组是与 current 形近或同出拉丁词干的词；第二组是都表示运动与方向、但「动的是什么」不同的词。

entries.definition: a small dried grape, from Old French raisins de Corauntz 'raisins of Corinth'; the spelling overlaps current but the root is a place name, not currere.
entries.definitionCN: 一种小葡萄干，其名来自古法语中「科林斯的葡萄干」一语；拼写与 current 重叠，但词根是地名，不是 currere。

entries.definition: current plus -cy: the state of being in circulation, hence the money that circulates and, more broadly, general acceptance.
entries.definitionCN: current 加 -cy：处于流通的状态，因此指流通的货币，更宽泛地也指被普遍接受。

entries.definition: from Latin cursus 'a running'; it keeps the route or track of the run rather than the water that runs along it.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cursus「奔跑」；它保留的是奔跑的路线或轨迹，而不是沿途奔跑的水。

entries.definition: Latin cursor 'runner'; on a screen it is the marker that runs across the text, so the old runner survives in a new medium.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 cursor「奔跑者」；在屏幕上它是跑过文本的标记，古老的「奔跑者」于是活在新媒介里。

entries.definition: the steady movement of a fluid, without the sense of a defined channel or direction that current usually carries.
entries.definitionCN: 流体稳定的运动，不带 current 通常含有的「有固定通道或方向」之意。

entries.definition: a small river, or a narrow moving band of water; in oceanography a stream is a narrow current, so the words overlap at small scale.
entries.definitionCN: 小溪，或一条窄的流动水带；在海洋学中 stream 指窄流，两词在小尺度上重叠。

entries.definition: the twice-daily rise and fall of the sea; unlike a current it reverses and follows the moon rather than running in one direction.
entries.definitionCN: 海面每日两次的涨落；与 current 不同，它会反向，随月亮而行，而不是朝一个方向持续流动。

entries.definition: the general direction of change in data or opinion; it shares the figurative sense of current but never the water sense.
entries.definitionCN: 数据或舆论变化的总方向；它与 current 共享比喻义，却从不用来指水。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin currere 'to run': a current is water, air or charge that is running.
normal.cn: 拉丁 currere「跑」：current 就是正在跑的水、空气或电荷。

normal.en: The family runs current, currently, currency, undercurrent, countercurrent, occur, course, cursor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 current、currently、currency、undercurrent、countercurrent、occur、course、cursor。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the physical senses: ocean current, air current, electric current.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出物理义：洋流、气流、电流。

normal.en: The adjective sense is 'running now', which is why current affairs are affairs of the present.
normal.cn: 形容词义是「此刻正在跑的」，因此 current affairs 就是当下的时事。

normal.en: Currant is the trap: it comes from Corinth, not from currere.
normal.cn: currant 是陷阱：它来自科林斯这个地名，而不是 currere。

abstract.en: Picture a leaf that goes wherever the water decides.
abstract.cn: 想象一片叶子，去哪儿全由水决定。

abstract.en: Picture a needle that swings because a river of charge is passing through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根指针摆动，因为有一条电荷之河正穿过它。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence everyone repeats until it becomes the way things are said.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话被所有人重复，直到它成了事情的标准说法。

examples.en: A cold current runs along the western edge of the basin.
examples.cn: 一股寒流沿海盆西缘流动。

examples.en: The current reversed when the tide changed.
examples.cn: 潮水转向时，水流也反了方向。

examples.en: Under current law, the discharge is permitted.
examples.cn: 按现行法律，这种排放是被允许的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡润特」——河水「跑」个不停，正跑着的那股水就是 current，也正是「当前」 → 水流；电流；当前的

root: 拉丁 currere「跑」→ 现在分词 currens, current-「跑着的」→ 古法语 corant → 中古英语 current；水流、气流、电流都是「跑动之物」的引申，货币「流通」与法律「现行」则来自「仍在跑」；currere 的印欧来源一般重构为 *kers-「跑」，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one verb: something that runs. Water runs, air runs, charge runs, opinion runs in a direction, and whatever has not stopped running is present, in circulation or in force.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项追着同一个动词：跑。水在跑，空气在跑，电荷在跑，舆论朝某个方向跑；凡尚未停下的一切，就是当下的、流通的或现行的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stream that never stops running in one direction, carrying whatever floats in it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从不停下、始终朝一个方向奔跑的溪流，载着漂浮其中的一切。

branches.en: THE LITERAL RUN: the oldest layer is water in motion, and the adjective still says 'running' in literary prose.
branches.cn: 字面上的跑：最古老的一层是运动中的水，而形容词义在文学文字里仍说「流动的」。

branches.en: OTHER MEDIA: air and electric charge are read through the same stream image, because both behave like fluids.
branches.cn: 别的介质：空气与电荷都借同一个溪流意象来理解，因为两者都像流体一样行为。

branches.en: DIRECTION AND MOMENT: a tendency is a direction, and what runs on into now is the present.
branches.cn: 方向与时刻：趋势是一个方向，而一直跑到现在的东西就是当下。

branches.en: STILL MOVING THROUGH HANDS: money and words circulate, and a law still applied is still in force.
branches.cn: 仍在手中传递：货币与词语在流通，仍在被执行的法律就是现行有效。

branches.en: THE PERSON IN POST: the holder is the one whose term is running at this moment.
branches.cn: 在任的人：在任者就是此刻任期正在奔跑的那个人。

intro.en: Current is a Latin participle that became both a noun and an adjective; its family is built by adding English suffixes and prefixes to the same running stem.
intro.cn: current 是一个既作名词又作形容词的拉丁分词；它的词族都是在同一个「跑」的词干上加英语前缀与后缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Latin currere supplies currens and cursus; the same stem returns in English course, cursor, occur and currency.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 currere 提供 currens 与 cursus；同一词干在英语的 course、cursor、occur、currency 中重现。

items.structure: currere, curro, cucurri, cursus (v., third conjugation)
items.example: Currere is the source of a whole family of English words.
items.exampleCN: currere 是一整族英语单词的来源。

items.example: Aqua currens means running water.
items.exampleCN: aqua currens 意为流动的水。

items.example: Currens, patens and urgens share this ending.
items.exampleCN: currens、patens 与 urgens 共用这个后缀。

items.meaning: water, air or charge in motion; also the present
items.meaningCN: 流动的水、空气或电荷；亦指现在
items.example: The current runs faster after the rain.
items.exampleCN: 雨后水流更急。

items.example: The office is currently closed.
items.exampleCN: 该办事处目前关闭。

items.example: The currency lost half its value.
items.exampleCN: 该货币贬值一半。

items.meaning: a current below the surface; a hidden tendency
items.example: An undercurrent of worry ran through the room.
items.exampleCN: 房间里潜藏着一股忧虑。

items.example: Two countercurrents meet at the strait.
items.exampleCN: 两股反向水流在海峡相遇。

items.meaning: to run into one's path, hence to happen
items.meaningCN: 跑进某人的路上，因此指发生
items.example: Storms occur here in late summer.
items.exampleCN: 此地夏末有风暴。

items.structure: Latin cursus 'a running', via Old French cours
items.meaning: a direction or route of movement
items.example: The ship changed course at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 船在黎明改变航向。
